title: Pauline Jaricot (1799–1862)
hookLine: a young laywoman in Lyon organizes small groups that fund missions far beyond France

lines: A CITY OF SILK AND LOOMS.
cards: Lyon, France, a city of silk. In the workshops, women and girls stand at the looms for long days and small pay.

One young woman from a well-off family of silk merchants has had a change of heart and put away her fine dresses. Her brother, studying for the priesthood, writes home about missionaries far away and how little they have.
She can't send much herself. But she has an idea about the women at the looms. Not one big gift from one rich person.
Something tiny, from many hands, every week.

teach.h: A COIN A WEEK, AND A PRAYER.
teach.b: Her name was Pauline Jaricot. She was not a nun, and never became one; she stayed a laywoman her whole life. First, the circle.
She asked a small group of friends and workers to give a small coin each week, and to pray for the missions. Each of them gathered a small group of their own. Groups fed into groups.
Out of this work came the Society for the Propagation of the Faith, which Catholics still support today when a collection is taken up for the missions. Third, the smallest coin.

In Mark's Gospel, Jesus watches a poor widow drop two tiny coins into the temple treasury, and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "this poor widow hath cast in more than all they who have cast into the treasury."
In the Latin of the Vulgate, her two coins are duo minuta. Pauline couldn't cross the ocean; neither could the women at the looms. But a small coin, given again and again, could.

teach.h: A FAILED VENTURE, A POOR DEATH.
teach.b: Later in life she put money into a venture meant to give workers decent jobs and a decent life. It failed. People she trusted let her down, and she died in debt and poverty.
The Church did not forget her; it later declared her blessed.
Her story asks what a small group of ordinary people can do, if each gives a little and keeps giving. Her answer reached far beyond Lyon, though she never saw the places those coins went.

how: Catholic parishes hold a yearly collection for the missions, World Mission Sunday, which supports the Society for the Propagation of the Faith; some Catholics also give a small amount each month through mission societies.

games.q: you want to help missionaries far away, but you can't send much yourself. what do you do?
o: wait until you are rich enough to give a large gift.
gather friends who each give a small coin weekly, and pray.
games.why: she gathered small groups, each member giving a little every week. the groups grew into the Society for the Propagation of the Faith.

practice: Hold a coin in your hand, or picture one, and feel how small it is. Think of where it might go: a clinic, a school, a kitchen, a family you will never meet.
If you pray, pray for people working far from home for others; if you don't, simply wish them well.
